@luduvo/server/global/NumberSequence.documentation: NumberSequence creates a number curve over time from 0 to 1, such as the size of a particle over its life. A sequence has 2 to 8 keypoints, and values change in a straight line between them. To read the keypoints, see `NumberSequence`.

@luduvo/server/global/NumberSequence.new.documentation: `NumberSequence.new` creates a sequence of one number, a ramp from `n0` to `n1`, or a sequence from a list of `NumberSequenceKeypoint` values. A list must start at time 0, end at time 1 and be in time order.
@luduvo/server/global/NumberSequence.new.code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: particles that shrink to nothing.
local puffs = Instance.new("Puffs")
puffs:AddComponent("ParticleEmitter", "ParticleSpawnRate", "ParticleSizeCurve")
puffs.ParticleSizeCurve.Curve = NumberSequence.new(1, 0)
puffs.Parent = self

@luduvo/server/global/NumberSequenceKeyp.documentation: NumberSequenceKeypoint creates one point of a `NumberSequence`. To read a keypoint, see `NumberSequenceKeypoint`.
`NumberSequenceKeypoint.new` creates a keypoint with `value` at `time`, from 0 to 1. The optional `envelope` lets values read from the curve vary at random by up to that much above or below `value`.
@luduvo/server/global/NumberSequenceKeyp.code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: embers whose peak opacity varies from 0.5 to 1.
local embers = Instance.new("Embers")
embers:AddComponent("ParticleEmitter", "ParticleSpawnRate", "ParticleColorRamp")
embers.ParticleColorRamp.Opacity = NumberSequence.new({
    NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0, 0.5),
    NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0.5, 0.75, 0.25),
    NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(1, 0),
})
embers.Parent = self

@luduvo/server/global/Rect.documentation: Rect creates a 2D rectangle from the pixel positions of two corners, such as an image's `SliceCenter`. In `CornerRadii`, the four numbers are the top-left, top-right, bottom-right and bottom-left corner radii. To read a rectangle, see `Rect`.

@luduvo/server/global/Rect.new.code_sample:
-- Client script: a panel with rounded top corners only.
local hud = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
hud.Parent = game.Overlay

local panel = Instance.new("Frame")
panel.UIRect.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(300, 200)
panel.CornerRadii = Rect.new(16, 16, 0, 0)
panel.Parent = hud

@luduvo/server/global/UDim.documentation: UDim creates one axis of an interface size or position: a share of the parent's size plus pixels. To read one, see `UDim`.

@luduvo/server/global/UDim.new.documentation: `UDim.new` creates an axis from a scale and a pixel offset. Scripts usually build both axes at once with `UDim2.new` and use `UDim` to compare one axis.
@luduvo/server/global/UDim.new.code_sample:
-- Client script.
local hud = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
hud.Parent = game.Overlay

local bar = Instance.new("Frame")
bar.UIRect.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 48)
bar.Parent = hud
print(bar.UIRect.Size.X == UDim.new(1, 0)) -- prints true

@luduvo/server/global/UDim2.documentation: UDim2 creates the position or size of an interface element. Each axis is a scale, a share of the parent's size where 1 is 100%, plus an offset in pixels. To read one, see `UDim2`.

@luduvo/server/global/UDim2.fromOffset.documentation: `UDim2.fromOffset` creates a `UDim2` from pixel offsets alone.
@luduvo/server/global/UDim2.fromOffset.code_sample:
-- Client script: a 96 by 96 pixel frame 20 pixels from the top left.
local hud = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
hud.Parent = game.Overlay

local portrait = Instance.new("Frame")
portrait.UIRect.Position = UDim2.fromOffset(20, 20)
portrait.UIRect.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(96, 96)
portrait.Parent = hud

@luduvo/server/global/UDim2.fromScale.code_sample:
-- Client script: a frame that covers the right half of the screen.
local hud = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
hud.Parent = game.Overlay

local pane = Instance.new("Frame")
pane.UIRect.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0)
pane.UIRect.Size = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 1)
pane.Parent = hud

@luduvo/server/global/UDim2.new.code_sample:
-- Client script: a sidebar 240 pixels wide and as tall as the screen.
local hud = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
hud.Parent = game.Overlay

local sidebar = Instance.new("Frame")
sidebar.UIRect.Position = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 0)
sidebar.UIRect.Size = UDim2.new(0, 240, 1, 0)
sidebar.Parent = hud

@luduvo/server/global/Vector2.documentation: Vector2 creates 2D vectors for interface positions and texture coordinates. A 2D vector is a Luau `vector` with `Z` set to 0, so it has the properties, methods and operators of a `Vector3`.

@luduvo/server/global/Vector2.new.code_sample:
-- Client script: a label centered on the screen.
local hud = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
hud.Parent = game.Overlay

local label = Instance.new("TextLabel")
label.Text = "Ready?"
label.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
label.UIRect.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.5)
label.Parent = hud

@luduvo/server/global/Vector3.documentation: Vector3 creates 3D vectors for positions, directions and sizes, in units. A vector is a Luau `vector`: read `X`, `Y` and `Z`, its length as `Magnitude` and its direction as `Unit`, and call `:Dot`, `:Cross` and `:Lerp` with a colon. Arithmetic works one component at a time, and `*` and `/` also scale by a number. Luau's `vector` library works on these values too; read `Unit` rather than `vector.normalize` when a vector can be zero, because `Vector3.zero.Unit` is `Vector3.zero` while `vector.normalize(Vector3.zero)` is NaN.
@luduvo/server/global/Vector3.code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local offset = Vector3.new(3, 0, 4)
print(offset.Magnitude) -- prints 5
print(offset:Dot(Vector3.xAxis)) -- prints 3
self.Position = self.Position + offset.Unit * 10

@luduvo/server/global/Vector3.new.code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
self.Position = Vector3.new(0, 10, 0)

@luduvo/server/global/Vector3.one.documentation:
`Vector3.one` is the vector with every component 1.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/Vector3.xAxis.documentation:
`Vector3.xAxis` is the unit vector along +X.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/Vector3.yAxis.documentation:
`Vector3.yAxis` is the unit vector along +Y, which points up.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/Vector3.zAxis.documentation:
`Vector3.zAxis` is the unit vector along +Z.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/Vector3.zero.documentation:
`Vector3.zero` is the vector with every component 0.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Animation.documentation:
Animation has the numbers scripts need to write a character's AnimLayers: the first layer scripts may write and the limb mask flags. Layers 1 through 4 play the built-in clips `idle`, `walk`, `jump`, `tread`, `swim`, `sit`, `climb`, and `hang`; layers FirstScriptLayer through 8 are free for scripts.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Animation.Dra.documentation:
DrainMarkers returns the clip markers that playback crossed.

Server only.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Animation.Fir.documentation:
FirstScriptLayer is the lowest AnimLayers index a script may write. Writing a lower layer raises an error.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Animation.Par.documentation:
Part has the limb flags for the `mask` of an animation layer. A masked layer moves only those limbs; the rest of the body keeps playing the lower layers.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Bool.documentation:
Bool is the field type of a boolean. Any value other than false and nil is sent as true.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.CloudStore.documentation:
CloudStore saves player data in the cloud, where every server of the place can read it. Use Store when the data stays on one server machine.

Server only.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.CloudStore.op.documentation:
open opens the key-value store `name` and returns its `CloudStore` handle. Opening the same name again returns the same store.

Server only.
@luduvo/server/global/game.CloudStore.op.code_sample:
-- Server script.
local profiles = game.CloudStore.open("player_profiles")

game.Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
    -- save a starting profile for each player who joins
    profiles:put(tostring(player.UserId), { gold = 100 }, nil, function(version, err)
        if not version then
            warn(err)
        end
    end)
end)

@luduvo/server/global/game.CloudStore.op.documentation:
open_ordered opens the leaderboard store `name` and returns its `OrderedCloudStore` handle. An ordered store maps each key to a whole-number score and reads keys sorted by score; opening the same name again returns the same store.

Server only.
notes: Ordered stores work only on a local test server, which keeps them in memory. On an online server every ordered call fails in its callback.
@luduvo/server/global/game.CloudStore.op.code_sample:
-- Server script.
local highScores = game.CloudStore.open_ordered("weekly_high_scores")

game.Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
    -- record a score of 0 for each player who joins
    highScores:set(tostring(player.UserId), 0, function(ok, err)
        if not ok then
            warn(err)
        end
    end)
end)

@luduvo/server/global/game.Color.documentation:
Color is the field type of an RGB color with 8 bits per channel. Each component of a sent vector clamps to 0 to 1.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Content.documentation:
Content downloads published assets by id, spawns downloaded scenes, and looks up player avatars and headshots. An asset id is a decimal string that names a published scene, mesh, texture, or audio clip; for prefabs saved with the place, use Prefabs.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Content.Avata.documentation:
Avatar looks up the avatar a player wears and returns a `ContentRequest` handle. The callback receives a manifest table with `UserId`, `Body` and `BodyColors` (keyed by `"Head"`, `"Torso"`, `"LeftArm"`, `"RightArm"`, `"LeftLeg"`, and `"RightLeg"`), `Face`, `Shirt`, `Pants`, and up to 24 `Accessories` (`Asset`, `Slot`, `Sha256`).

Server only.
notes: The callback receives `nil, nil` when the player has no platform account, or on a local playtest server when the player is not the signed-in editor.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Content.Avata.code_sample:
-- Server script.
game.Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
    game.Content.Avatar(player, function(manifest, _err)
        -- nil on error or when the player has no avatar
        if not manifest then
            return
        end
        for _, item in manifest.Accessories do
            game.Content.Fetch(item.Asset, item.Sha256, function(asset, _fetchErr)
                local character = player.Character
                if asset and character then
                    character:AddAccessory(asset)
                end
            end)
        end
    end)
end)

@luduvo/server/global/game.Content.Fetch.documentation: Fetch downloads an asset into the memory cache and returns a `ContentRequest` handle. The callback receives a `ContentAsset`, or `nil` and an error string.
notes: The callback runs on a later frame, even when the asset is already cached.
The cache keeps up to 128 assets and 32 MiB of scenes, and drops the least recently used asset when full. A larger scene fails with `"the asset is larger than the memory the runtime holds"`.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Content.Fetch.code_sample:
-- Server script.
-- pass nil to skip the SHA-256 check
local request = game.Content.Fetch("1000000000000001", nil, function(asset, err)
    if not asset then
        warn("Fetch failed: " .. tostring(err))
        return
    end
    if asset.Type == "scene" then
        game.Content.Spawn(asset)
    end
end)

-- give up if the download takes longer than 10 seconds
task.delay(10, function()
    if request.Pending then
        request:Cancel()
    end
end)

@luduvo/server/global/game.Content.Heads.documentation: Headshot returns the texture asset id of a user's headshot portrait, or `""` when `userId` is 0 or less. The user does not need to be in the server.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Content.Heads.code_sample:
-- Server script.
local hud = Instance.new("HUD")
hud.UIRoot = true
hud.UIRect.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, 0)
hud.Parent = game.World

local slots = 0
game.Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
    local portrait = Instance.new("ImageLabel")
    portrait.UIRect.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(96, 96)
    portrait.UIRect.Position = UDim2.fromOffset(20 + slots * 104, 20)
    -- the label draws nothing until the portrait downloads
    portrait.Image = game.Content.Headshot(player.UserId)
    portrait.Parent = hud
    slots += 1
end)

@luduvo/server/global/game.Content.Spawn.documentation:
Spawn creates the instance tree of a fetched scene and returns its root. It returns `nil` when the asset is not a scene or was dropped from the cache.

Server only.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Content.Spawn.code_sample:
-- Server script.
game.Content.Fetch("1000000000000001", nil, function(asset, _err)
    if asset and asset.Type == "scene" then
        local root = game.Content.Spawn(asset)
        if root then
            -- place the spawned scene 10 units up
            root.Position = Vector3.new(0, 10, 0)
        end
    end
end)

@luduvo/server/global/game.Csg.documentation:
Csg combines parts into one solid shape, called a union, and takes unions apart again. A union draws one outer surface and collides as one body.

Server only.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Csg.Intersect.documentation:
Intersect replaces the parts with one union that keeps only the volume they all share.

Server only.
notes: Returns `nil, "result is empty"` when the parts do not overlap.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Csg.Intersect.code_sample:
-- Server script.
local left = Instance.new("Part")
left.Anchored = true
left.Position = Vector3.new(0, 5, 0)

local right = Instance.new("Part")
right.Anchored = true
right.Position = Vector3.new(2, 5, 0)

-- keep only the overlap of the two boxes
local overlap, err = game.Csg.Intersect({ left, right })
if not overlap then
    warn("intersect failed: " .. (err or ""))
end

@luduvo/server/global/game.Csg.Negate.documentation:
Negate wraps each part in a negative instance named `"Negate"` that cuts the part's volume out of any union it joins. Outside a union, a negative instance draws translucent pink and does not collide.

Server only.
notes: Passing a negative instance unwraps its part instead, like Separate.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Csg.Negate.code_sample:
-- Server script.
local wall = Instance.new("Part")
wall.Anchored = true
wall.Size = Vector3.new(12, 8, 1)
wall.Position = Vector3.new(0, 4, 0)

local window = Instance.new("Part")
window.Anchored = true
window.Size = Vector3.new(3, 3, 2)
window.Position = Vector3.new(0, 5, 0)

-- turn the window into a hole, then join it with the wall
local holes = game.Csg.Negate({ window })
if holes then
    table.insert(holes, 1, wall)
    game.Csg.Union(holes)
end

@luduvo/server/global/game.Csg.Separate.documentation:
Separate destroys a union or negative instance after moving its children to its parent, and returns the children.

Server only.
notes: If the union was resized, the stretch is applied to the children's positions and sizes.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Csg.Separate.code_sample:
-- Server script.
local a = Instance.new("Part")
a.Anchored = true
local b = Instance.new("Part")
b.Anchored = true
b.Position = Vector3.new(4, 0, 0)

local union = game.Csg.Union({ a, b })
if union then
    -- break the union back into its parts
    local pieces = game.Csg.Separate(union)
    if pieces then
        for _, piece in pieces do
            piece.Name = "Debris"
        end
    end
end

@luduvo/server/global/game.Csg.Subtract.documentation:
Subtract cuts `cutters` out of `main` and returns one union of what remains, such as a wall with a doorway. The union takes `main`'s parent, rotation, color, material, and anchoring.

Server only.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Csg.Subtract.code_sample:
-- Server script.
local wall = Instance.new("Part")
wall.Anchored = true
wall.Size = Vector3.new(12, 8, 1)
wall.Position = Vector3.new(0, 4, 0)

local doorway = Instance.new("Part")
doorway.Anchored = true
doorway.Size = Vector3.new(4, 6, 2)
doorway.Position = Vector3.new(0, 3, 0)

-- cut the doorway out of the wall
local cut, err = game.Csg.Subtract(wall, { doorway })
if cut then
    cut.Name = "WallWithDoor"
else
    warn("doorway failed: " .. (err or ""))
end

@luduvo/server/global/game.Csg.Union.documentation:
Union joins parts into one union that draws and collides as a single solid. The parts move inside the union and keep their identity, so existing references to them stay valid.

Server only.
notes: Returns `nil` and `"union is too complex (<triangles> triangles, limit 20000)"` when the surface needs too many triangles; use fewer parts or fewer round parts.
Returns `nil` and `"too many operands (limit 4096)"` when the call names too many parts.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Csg.Union.code_sample:
-- Server script.
local left = Instance.new("Part")
left.Anchored = true
left.Size = Vector3.new(1, 6, 1)
left.Position = Vector3.new(-3, 3, 0)

local right = Instance.new("Part")
right.Anchored = true
right.Size = Vector3.new(1, 6, 1)
right.Position = Vector3.new(3, 3, 0)

local beam = Instance.new("Part")
beam.Anchored = true
beam.Size = Vector3.new(7, 1, 1)
beam.Position = Vector3.new(0, 6.5, 0)

-- join two posts and a beam into one arch
local arch, err = game.Csg.Union({ left, right, beam })
if arch then
    arch.Name = "Arch"
else
    warn("arch failed: " .. (err or ""))
end

@luduvo/server/global/game.Emoji.documentation:
Emoji looks up the built-in emojis by shortcode, picker category, and search words. A shortcode is an emoji's lowercase name without colons, such as `"+1"` or `"pirate_flag"`. A skin tone is a number from 1, the default yellow, to 6.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Emoji.Categor.documentation: Categories returns the eight picker categories in display order, each with `id`, `name`, and `count`. The first, `"frequent"`, is empty; fill it from the player's picks or from FrequentDefaults.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Emoji.Categor.code_sample:
-- Client script.
for _, category in game.Emoji.Categories() do
    print(category.id .. ": " .. category.count) -- first prints "frequent: 0"
end

@luduvo/server/global/game.Emoji.Categor.documentation: CategoryAt returns the shortcode at a position in a category, or `nil` past the end of the category.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Emoji.Categor.code_sample:
-- Client script: list the first ten emojis of "people", category 2.
for i = 1, 10 do
    print(game.Emoji.CategoryAt(2, i)) -- first prints "grinning"
end

@luduvo/server/global/game.Emoji.Frequen.documentation: FrequentDefaults returns the eight shortcodes the frequently used category shows before the player picks any emoji.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Emoji.Frequen.code_sample:
-- Client script.
local defaults = game.Emoji.FrequentDefaults()
print(#defaults .. " defaults, first " .. defaults[1]) -- prints "8 defaults, first +1"

@luduvo/server/global/game.Emoji.Glyph.documentation: Glyph returns the text of an emoji in a skin tone and whether the emoji has skin tones. For an unknown shortcode, the text is `nil`.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Emoji.Glyph.code_sample:
-- Client script: a label that shows a thumbs-up in skin tone 3.
local label = Instance.new("TextLabel")
local glyph, hasTones = game.Emoji.Glyph("+1", 3)
label.Text = glyph or ""
print(hasTones) -- prints "true"

@luduvo/server/global/game.Emoji.Info.documentation: Info returns the text and display name of an emoji in a skin tone, or `nil` twice for an unknown shortcode.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Emoji.Info.code_sample:
-- Client script.
local _, name = game.Emoji.Info("heart_eyes")
print(name) -- prints "Smiling Face with Heart-Eyes"

@luduvo/server/global/game.Emoji.Search.documentation: Search returns up to `limit` shortcodes, 90 by default, of emojis where each word of the query starts a word in the name or keywords, best match first. It returns `nil` when the query has no words.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Entity.documentation:
Entity is the same token as Instance.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.EventTable.documentation:
EventTable declares a network event table that sends events between the server and clients, such as a player's request to attack or the server's report of a hit. It returns an EventTable handle for firing and reading events.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.F32.documentation:
F32 is the field type of a 32-bit float. A sent number is rounded to a 32-bit float, and in a `ToServer` event the server drops the packet on NaN or infinity.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.I32.documentation:
I32 is the field type of a signed 32-bit whole number. A sent number loses its fraction.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Instance.documentation:
Instance is the field type of a reference to an instance, or nil. A read returns the receiver's instance with the same network ID, or nil when it does not exist there.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Items.documentation:
Items checks the bytes of a saved place, model, or accessory file without changing the running world.

Server only.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Items.Examine.documentation:
Examine loads `.ldv` file bytes into a temporary world, destroys that world, and returns a table of facts about them. Damaged bytes give `loaded = false` instead of an error.

Server only.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Items.Examine.code_sample:
-- Server script: refuse model bytes that are too big or have scripts.
local function safeModel(bytes: string): boolean
    local facts = game.Items.Examine("model", bytes)
    if not facts.loaded or facts.entities > 50 then
        return false
    end
    for _, ent in facts.ents do
        if ent.script then
            return false
        end
    end
    return true
end

print(safeModel("not an ldv file")) -- prints false

@luduvo/server/global/game.Lighting.documentation:
Lighting has the place-wide sun, ambient light, sky, clouds, fog and camera exposure. For lamps on parts, add `Light` or `SpotCone` instead.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Lighting.Ambi.documentation:
Ambient is the indirect light on surfaces in shadow.

Read only at runtime.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Lighting.Ambi.code_sample:
-- Server script: dim blue night light.
local amb = game.Lighting.Ambient
amb.Source = "Color"
amb.Tint = Vector3.new(0.3, 0.35, 0.5)
amb.Intensity = 0.2

@luduvo/server/global/game.Lighting.Atmo.documentation:
AtmosphereSky is a deprecated group; `AtmosphereSky` on the Environment has no settings.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Lighting.Back.documentation:
Background is the color behind the scene when there is no sky, and the brightness of the background and sky.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Lighting.Clou.documentation:
Clouds is the volumetric cloud layer, drawn in front of every kind of sky.

Read only at runtime.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Lighting.Clou.code_sample:
-- Server script: an overcast sky.
local clouds = game.Lighting.Clouds
clouds.Coverage = 0.9
clouds.BottomDarkening = 0.5

@luduvo/server/global/game.Lighting.Expo.documentation:
Exposure is the range of the camera's automatic exposure, in exposure values (EV). The camera picks an EV between `MinEV` and `MaxEV` from the brightness in view; equal values fix the exposure.

Read only at runtime.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Lighting.Expo.code_sample:
-- Server script: fixed exposure for a cave level.
local exposure = game.Lighting.Exposure
exposure.MinEV = 5
exposure.MaxEV = 5

@luduvo/server/global/game.Lighting.Flar.documentation:
Flare is the lens flare and sun rays that show when the camera faces the sun.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Lighting.Fog.documentation:
Fog is the distance fog that fades far parts into a color. It leaves the sky clear.

Read only at runtime.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Lighting.Fog.code_sample:
-- Server script: thick fog that hides parts past 80 units.
local fog = game.Lighting.Fog
fog.Mode = "Linear"
fog.Start = 10
fog.End = 80
fog.Color = Vector3.new(0.7, 0.75, 0.8)

@luduvo/server/global/game.Lighting.Pano.documentation:
PanoramaSky is a sky drawn from one panorama or cube texture.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Lighting.Shad.documentation:
Shadows is how the sun casts shadows.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Lighting.SixS.documentation:
SixSidedSky is a sky drawn from six square face textures.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Lighting.Star.documentation:
Stars is a deprecated group; the atmosphere sky draws no stars.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Lighting.Sun.documentation:
Sun is the direction, color and strength of sunlight. Writing `Azimuth` or `Elevation` turns the Sun instance.

Read only at runtime.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Lighting.Sun.code_sample:
-- Server script: the sun circles the sky once every 2 minutes.
function Update(dt: number)
    local sun = game.Lighting.Sun
    sun.Azimuth = (sun.Azimuth + dt * 3) % 360
end

@luduvo/server/global/game.Lighting.SunD.documentation:
SunDisk is the size of the sun's disk in an atmosphere sky. A panorama or six-sided sky draws whatever sun its texture has.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Locale.documentation:
Locale gets and sets the player's language and translates text into it. Only clients have a language; on the server `Get` returns `"en"`, `Set` returns `false` and `"unavailable"`, and `Translate` returns its key.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Locale.Get.documentation: Get returns the active language tag, `"en"` until something changes it.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Locale.Get.code_sample:
-- Client script.
local lang = game.Locale.Get()
if lang == "ja" or string.sub(lang, 1, 2) == "zh" then
    print("use a CJK font")
end

@luduvo/server/global/game.Locale.Set.documentation: Set switches the active language. It returns `true` and `"changed"` or `"unchanged"`, or `false` and `"rejected"` when the tag is not valid.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Locale.Set.code_sample:
-- Client script.
local ok, status = game.Locale.Set("pt-BR")
if not ok then
    warn("cannot switch language: " .. status)
end

@luduvo/server/global/game.Locale.Transl.documentation: Translate returns the translation of an English key in the active language, or the key itself when there is none.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Locale.Transl.code_sample:
-- Client script.
local template = game.Locale.Translate("Welcome, {name}!")
print((string.gsub(template, "{name}", "Ana")))

@luduvo/server/global/game.Marketplace.documentation:
Marketplace sells the products of your place for Lunes, the platform currency. You create products and set their prices on the website, a script shows the purchase prompt, and the server grants what the player bought.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Marketplace.G.documentation: GetSubscriptionStatus returns a player's subscription to a product of this place as a `SubscriptionStatus` table. `Active` is `false` when the player has no subscription to the product.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Marketplace.G.code_sample:
-- Server script in a gate part.
local SEASON_PASS = 9012

-- mark season members when they touch the gate
self.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
    local player = game.Players.FromCharacter(hit)
    if player then
        local status = game.Marketplace.GetSubscriptionStatus(player, SEASON_PASS)
        player.attr.SeasonMember = status.Active
    end
end)

@luduvo/server/global/game.Marketplace.O.documentation: OwnsProduct returns whether a player owns a durable product or has an active subscription to a product of this place. A consumable is never owned.
notes: Answers from what the server last fetched from Luduvo: on join, after each of the player's prompts closes, and when a subscription period ends. Right after a join a player owns nothing for a moment.
A modified client can fake its own products, so check ownership on the server.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Marketplace.O.code_sample:
-- Server script in a door part.
local VIP_PASS = 5678

-- fade the door for players who own the VIP pass
self.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
    local player = game.Players.FromCharacter(hit)
    if player and game.Marketplace.OwnsProduct(player, VIP_PASS) then
        self.Transparency = 0.5
    end
end)

@luduvo/server/global/game.Marketplace.P.documentation: ProcessReceipt is the callback that grants a bought consumable. Set it to a function that takes a `ProductReceipt` and returns `true` once the player has what they paid for.
notes: Only a return of `true` marks the receipt delivered. Any other return, an error, or a yield such as `task.wait` leaves it undelivered, and the server passes it again later.
Runs for every undelivered receipt of a player when the player joins and after each of that player's prompts closes.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Marketplace.P.code_sample:
-- Server script.
local COINS_PRODUCT = 1234

-- give 100 coins for each coin pack bought
game.Marketplace.ProcessReceipt = function(receipt)
    local player = game.Players.Get(receipt.PlayerId)
    if player and receipt.ProductId == COINS_PRODUCT then
        player.attr.Coins = (player.attr.Coins or 0) + 100
        return true
    end
    return false
end

@luduvo/server/global/game.Marketplace.P.documentation:
ProductType is the table of `ProductType` tokens (`Consumable`, `Durable`, and `Subscription`) passed to `PromptProductPurchase`.

Read only at runtime.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Marketplace.P.code_sample:
-- Server script.
local SEASON_PASS = 9012

-- offer a monthly or yearly subscription
game.Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
    game.Marketplace.PromptProductPurchase(player, SEASON_PASS,
        game.Marketplace.ProductType.Subscription)
end)

@luduvo/server/global/game.Marketplace.P.documentation: PromptProductPurchase shows the purchase prompt for a product of this place to a player. The product type defaults to `Marketplace.ProductType.Consumable`.
notes: A request while a prompt is open, or within 2 seconds after the last one closed, opens nothing and fires `PromptProductPurchaseFinished` with `purchased` set to `false`.
In Studio Play the prompt is a test purchase and spends no Lunes.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Marketplace.P.code_sample:
-- Server script.
local VIP_PASS = 5678

-- offer the VIP pass to every player who joins
game.Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
    game.Marketplace.PromptProductPurchase(player, VIP_PASS,
        game.Marketplace.ProductType.Durable)
end)

@luduvo/server/global/game.Marketplace.P.documentation:
PromptProductPurchaseFinished fires when a purchase prompt closes, passing the player, the product id, and whether the player bought the product.

Read only at runtime.
notes: Fires on both the client and the server, and the server event comes from the client. Use this signal only to update a shop UI; grant rewards in `ProcessReceipt` or after `OwnsProduct`.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Marketplace.P.code_sample:
-- Client script.
-- react when the local player closes a prompt without buying
game.Marketplace.PromptProductPurchaseFinished:Connect(
    function(player: Instance, productId: number, purchased: boolean)
        if not purchased then
            print(player.Name, "closed the prompt for", productId)
        end
    end)

@luduvo/server/global/game.Materials.documentation:
Materials lists, reads, defines, and removes the surface materials of a place. A material sets how its parts look, collide, and sound. A material with a `Shader` draws its parts with a shader from the project's `shaders` folder; see Writing a material shader.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Materials.Def.documentation:
DefineMaterial defines a material, or redefines the one with the same `Id`, and returns its asset id. Without a `Name`, the material gets the next free name.

Server only.
notes: Passing `parent`, a material asset id, saves it in the material file. When the file loads, every table that `spec` leaves out comes from `parent`.
Updates the material's surfaces and their physics. When the server runs from a project, it also writes the material file to the project's `materials` folder.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Materials.Get.documentation: GetMaterial returns the MaterialSpec of a material by asset id or name, in the form `DefineMaterial` takes.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Materials.Get.code_sample:
-- Server script.
local spec = game.Materials.GetMaterial("Plastic")

-- Surface can be nil
if spec.Surface then
    local roughness = spec.Surface.RoughnessMult
end

@luduvo/server/global/game.Materials.Get.documentation: GetMaterials returns an array of MaterialEntry tables with the asset id, name, pipeline, and surface model of every material in the place.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Materials.Get.code_sample:
-- Server script.
local materials = game.Materials.GetMaterials()

-- count the materials in this place
local count = #materials

@luduvo/server/global/game.Materials.Rel.documentation:
ReloadMaterial reads a material file from the project's `materials` folder again and redefines the material with it. Its surfaces keep the material.

Server only.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Materials.Rel.code_sample:
-- Server script, after editing materials/Lagoon in the project.
game.Materials.ReloadMaterial("Lagoon")

@luduvo/server/global/game.Materials.Rem.documentation:
RemoveMaterial removes a material and moves its surfaces to `replacementIdOrName`, or when that is omitted, to the material's parent or `Plastic`.

Server only.
notes: When the server runs from a project, deletes the material file from the project's `materials` folder.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Materials.Rem.code_sample:
-- Server script.
game.Materials.DefineMaterial({
    Id = "2810246167479189505",
    Name = "OldBrick",
    Pipeline = "Opaque",
    Model = "UV",
    Surface = {},
})

-- parts made of OldBrick now use Plastic
game.Materials.RemoveMaterial("OldBrick", "Plastic")

@luduvo/server/global/game.Materials.Rep.documentation:
ReplaceMaterial moves every surface from one material to another and removes the first.

Server only.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Materials.Rep.code_sample:
-- Server script.
game.Materials.DefineMaterial({
    Id = "2810246167479189505",
    Name = "CrackedConcrete",
    Pipeline = "Opaque",
    Model = "UV",
    Surface = {},
})

-- move every CrackedConcrete surface to Plastic
game.Materials.ReplaceMaterial("CrackedConcrete", "Plastic")

@luduvo/server/global/game.Navigation.documentation:
Navigation finds walkable paths across the place and walks characters along them, around walls, up ramps, and through doorways.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Navigation.Ag.documentation: AgentHeight is the lowest ceiling a path passes under, in units. It must be above 0 and at most 255 times `CellHeight`.
AgentMaxClimb is the highest step a path climbs, in units. It must be above 0 and at most `AgentHeight`.
AgentMaxSlope is the steepest slope a path walks up, in degrees, above 0 and below 90.
AgentRadius is how far paths keep from walls and edges, in units. It must be above 0 and at most 64 times `CellSize`.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Navigation.Ce.documentation: CellHeight is the height of one mesh cell, from 0.05 to 4 units.
CellSize is the width of one mesh cell, from 0.05 to 4 units. Smaller cells follow walls more closely and take longer to build.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Navigation.Co.documentation:
ComputePath returns a `PathStatus` and up to 256 corners along the shortest walkable path between `from` and `to`, filling `out` when given. `Success` reaches `to`, `ClosestNoPath` ends at the reachable point closest to `to`, and `NoPath` returns an empty array.

Server only.
notes: Looks for the mesh within twice `AgentRadius` sideways and `AgentHeight` above or below each point, so pass points on or slightly above the floor.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Navigation.Co.code_sample:
-- Server script.
local floor = Instance.new("Part")
floor.Anchored = true
floor.Size = Vector3.new(100, 1, 100)

-- pass a table to fill so repeated queries can reuse it
local corners: {vector} = {}
local status = game.Navigation.ComputePath(
    Vector3.new(-40, 1, -40),
    Vector3.new(40, 1, 40),
    corners
)
if status == "Success" then
    local marker = Instance.new("Part")
    marker.Anchored = true
    marker.Position = corners[#corners]
end

@luduvo/server/global/game.Navigation.Mo.documentation:
MoveTo walks `character` along the shortest walkable path to `target` and returns its `PathStatus` (see ComputePath). Calling it again replaces the path.

Server only.
notes: The walk ends when `PathFollower.Status` becomes `Arrived` or `Stuck`, when the character dies, or when Stop is called. On `NoPath` the character stays where it is.
When the mesh changes along the path, the character plans again from where it is, and stops if no path remains.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Navigation.Mo.code_sample:
-- Server script.
local floor = Instance.new("Part")
floor.Anchored = true
floor.Size = Vector3.new(100, 1, 100)

-- a custom NPC needs CharacterPhysics and Locomotion
local guard = Instance.new("Part")
guard.Position = Vector3.new(0, 3, 0)
guard:AddComponent("CharacterPhysics")
guard:AddComponent("Locomotion")

game.Navigation.MoveTo(guard, Vector3.new(30, 1, 30))

@luduvo/server/global/game.Navigation.St.documentation:
Stop ends the walk that MoveTo started and sets `PathFollower.Status` to `Idle`. It sets the move input to zero, so the character slows down like a player who releases the movement keys.

Server only.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Navigation.Ti.documentation: TileSize is the number of cells along one side of a mesh tile, from 16 to 256. A changed part rebuilds the tiles it touches, so smaller tiles rebuild faster.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Particles.documentation:
Particles plays and stops particle effects, and bursts and clears emitters. See particle effects for how to build them. A call on the server shows on every client; a call on a client shows on that client alone.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Particles.Cle.documentation: Clear removes every live particle of an emitter at once.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Particles.Cle.code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: three bursts of sparks, then clear them.
local sparks = Instance.new("Sparks")
sparks:AddComponent("ParticleEmitter", "ParticleShapeSphere",
    "ParticleVelocityCone", "ParticleSprite")
sparks.Parent = self

for i = 1, 3 do
    game.Particles.Emit(sparks, 32)
    task.wait(0.5)
end
game.Particles.Clear(sparks)

@luduvo/server/global/game.Particles.Emi.documentation: Emit spawns a burst of particles from an emitter, 16 when no count is given.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Particles.Emi.code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: burst 50 sparks.
local sparks = Instance.new("Sparks")
sparks:AddComponent("ParticleEmitter", "ParticleShapeSphere",
    "ParticleVelocityCone", "ParticleSprite")
sparks.Parent = self
game.Particles.Emit(sparks, 50)

@luduvo/server/global/game.Particles.Pla.documentation: Play starts a particle effect, or restarts it from the beginning.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Particles.Pla.code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: a flame that burns for 2 seconds.
local flame = Instance.new("Flame")
flame:AddComponent("ParticleEffect")
local embers = Instance.new("Embers")
embers:AddComponent("ParticleEmitter", "ParticleSpawnRate", "ParticleShapeSphere",
    "ParticleVelocityCone", "ParticleSprite")
embers.Parent = flame
flame.Parent = self

game.Particles.Play(flame)
task.wait(2)
game.Particles.Stop(flame, "Finish") -- live particles fade out

@luduvo/server/global/game.Particles.Pla.documentation: PlayAt spawns a particle effect at a world position and plays it. `effect` is a prefab name, an asset, or `"ParticleEmitter"` for default sparks. The new instance is removed after 5 seconds unless the prefab sets its own `Lifetime`.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Particles.Pla.code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: a 5-second stream of sparks at the part.
local sparks = game.Particles.PlayAt("ParticleEmitter", self.Position)
print(sparks.Name) -- prints ParticleEmitter

@luduvo/server/global/game.Particles.Sto.documentation: Stop stops a particle effect. `"Finish"`, the default, lets live particles fade out; `"Clear"` removes them at once.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Particles.Sto.code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: burn for 1 second, then clear live particles at once.
local flame = Instance.new("Flame")
flame:AddComponent("ParticleEffect")
local embers = Instance.new("Embers")
embers:AddComponent("ParticleEmitter", "ParticleSpawnRate", "ParticleShapeSphere",
    "ParticleVelocityCone", "ParticleSprite")
embers.Parent = flame
flame.Parent = self

game.Particles.Play(flame)
task.wait(1)
game.Particles.Stop(flame, "Clear")

@luduvo/server/global/game.Physics.documentation:
Physics has the place-wide simulation settings, the collision groups, and the spatial queries against collider shapes. The server and each client step their own physics world, and a call acts on the world of the side that makes it.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Physics.Drain.documentation: DrainTouchEvents returns the touches that began or ended since this script last called it.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Physics.Drain.deprecation: Connect `Instance.Touched` and `Instance.TouchEnded` on the part instead.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Physics.EmitA.documentation:
EmitAcousticStimulus makes a sound at `position` that listeners with `HearingSense` hear within `radius * loudness` units, scaled by each listener's sensitivity, and returns how many heard it. The `emitter` never hears itself.

Server only.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Physics.EmitA.code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local heard = game.Physics.EmitAcousticStimulus(self.Position, 20, 2, self)
print(heard)

@luduvo/server/global/game.Physics.Explo.documentation:
Explode breaks welds and pushes unanchored bodies away from `position` within `radius` units, and returns how many bodies it pushed. A negative `force` pulls bodies in.

Server only.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Physics.Explo.code_sample:
-- Server script in a grenade part.
task.wait(3)
game.Physics.Explode(self.Position, 15, 4000)
self:Destroy()

@luduvo/server/global/game.Physics.Falle.documentation:
FallenPartsDestroyHeight is the world Y below which moving parts are destroyed and characters die. Anchored parts are never destroyed this way.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Physics.Gravi.documentation: Gravity is the acceleration along the world Y axis, in units per second squared, that pulls every unanchored body. Negative values pull down. A server write replicates to clients.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Physics.IsSle.documentation: IsSleeping returns true when the physics body of `e` is at rest and the simulation skips it.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Physics.IsSle.code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local floor = Instance.new("Part")
floor.Size = Vector3.new(20, 1, 20)
floor.Position = Vector3.new(0, -2, 0)
floor.Anchored = true
floor.Parent = game.World

self.Anchored = false
task.wait(2)
print(game.Physics.IsSleeping(self)) -- prints true

@luduvo/server/global/game.Physics.Overl.documentation: OverlapBox returns the count and the entities whose shapes overlap a box with half size `half`, rotated by `rotation` in degrees.
OverlapSphere returns the count and the entities whose shapes overlap a sphere. It fills `out` when you pass one, so a script can reuse one table.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Physics.Rayca.documentation: Raycast returns the first surface hit from `origin` along `dir` within `maxDist` units, or nil. The hit has `Position`, `Normal`, `Instance` and `Distance`.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Physics.Rayca.code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local hit = game.Physics.Raycast(self.Position, Vector3.new(0, -1, 0), 1000, {
    ExcludeInstances = {self},
})
if hit and hit.Instance then
    print(hit.Instance.Name, hit.Distance)
end

@luduvo/server/global/game.Physics.Regis.documentation:
RegisterCollisionGroup adds a collision group named `name`. A part joins it when its `CollisionGroup` is set to that name. A new group collides with every group until `SetCollisionRule` changes that. A place has 32 group slots, and `Default`, `Character` and `CharacterNoCollide` take three of them.

Server only.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Physics.Regis.code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
game.Physics.RegisterCollisionGroup("Projectile")
game.Physics.SetCollisionRule("Projectile", "Projectile", false)
self.CollisionGroup = "Projectile"
print(self.CollisionGroup) -- prints Projectile

@luduvo/server/global/game.Physics.Renam.documentation:
RenameCollisionGroup renames group `from` to `to` and keeps its rules and parts.

Server only.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Physics.Renam.code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
game.Physics.RegisterCollisionGroup("TeamA")
self.CollisionGroup = "TeamA"
game.Physics.RenameCollisionGroup("TeamA", "Red")
print(self.CollisionGroup) -- prints Red

@luduvo/server/global/game.Physics.SetCo.documentation:
SetCollisionRule sets whether parts of group `a` collide with parts of group `b`. Pass the same group twice to set whether it collides with itself.

Server only.
notes: Spatial queries follow the rules only when their params name a `CollisionGroup`.
A character still stands on a part whose group does not collide with `Character`.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Physics.Shape.documentation: Shapecast sweeps a `"Box"`, `"Sphere"` or `"Capsule"` from `from` to `to` and returns the count and every hit, nearest first. Each hit has `Instance`, `Point`, `Normal` and `Fraction` (0 at `from`, 1 at `to`). For `"Box"`, `size` is half the size on each axis. For `"Sphere"`, `size.X` is the radius. For `"Capsule"`, `size.X` is the radius and `size.Y` is half the length of the straight middle.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Physics.Shape.code_sample:
-- Server script in a sword part.
local from = self.Position
local to = from + Vector3.new(0, 0, -5)
local n, hits = game.Physics.Shapecast("Box", Vector3.new(0.2, 0.2, 2), from, to, nil, nil, {
    ExcludeInstances = {self},
})
if n > 0 then
    print(hits[1].Instance.Name)
end

@luduvo/server/global/game.Players.documentation:
Players looks up players and their characters, fires signals when players join, leave, chat or spawn, and reports friend status.

Read only at runtime.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Players.code_sample:
-- Server script.
local red = Instance.new("Team")
red.Name = "Red"
red.TeamId = 1
red.TeamColor = Vector3.new(1, 0.25, 0.25)

local spectators = Instance.new("Team")
spectators.Name = "Spectators"
spectators.TeamId = 2
spectators:RemoveComponent("AutoAssignable")

@luduvo/server/global/game.Players.All.documentation: All returns every player in the session.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Players.BindC.documentation:
BindCharacter makes an instance the character of a player.

Server only.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Players.Chara.documentation:
CharacterAdded fires with a player and its new character. On the server, a `Position` set in the handler decides where the character appears.

Read only at runtime.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Players.Chara.code_sample:
-- Server script: spawn every character 50 units up.
game.Players.CharacterAdded:Connect(function(player, character)
    character.Position = Vector3.new(0, 50, 0)
end)

@luduvo/server/global/game.Players.Chara.documentation:
CharacterDied fires with the player, the character and the attacker when a character dies. The attacker is the one passed to the last `TakeDamage`, or nil. A fall below `FallenPartsDestroyHeight` clears the attacker.

Read only at runtime.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Players.Chara.code_sample:
-- Server script: count kills.
game.Players.CharacterDied:Connect(function(player, character, attacker)
    local killer = attacker and game.Players.FromCharacter(attacker)
    if killer and killer ~= player then
        killer.attr.Kills = (killer.attr.Kills or 0) + 1
    end
end)

@luduvo/server/global/game.Players.Chara.documentation: CharacterOf returns the character of a player, or nil.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Players.Frien.documentation: FriendStatus returns the relation of the local player to another player, one of the items of `game.Enum.FriendStatus`. It returns `"Unknown"` on the server.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Players.Frien.code_sample:
-- Client script.
for player in game.World.Each("Player") do
    if player ~= game.Players.LocalPlayer then
        print(player.Name, game.Players.FriendStatus(player))
    end
end

@luduvo/server/global/game.Players.FromC.documentation: FromCharacter returns the player that controls a character or one of its body parts, or nil.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Players.FromC.code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: mark players who touch it.
self.Touched:Connect(function(other)
    local player = game.Players.FromCharacter(other)
    if player then
        player.attr.Eliminated = true
    end
end)

@luduvo/server/global/game.Players.Get.documentation: Get returns the player with the given user ID, or nil.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Players.IsAdm.documentation: IsAdmin returns whether a player is an admin of the place.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Players.Kick.documentation:
Kick disconnects a player from the server and shows them the reason.

Server only.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Players.Kick.code_sample:
-- Server script.
game.Players.PlayerChatted:Connect(function(player, message)
    if message == "!leave" then
        game.Players.Kick(player, "Goodbye")
    end
end)

@luduvo/server/global/game.Players.Local.documentation:
LocalPlayer is the player of this client, or nil on the server and before the player reaches the client. The server owns the player, so a client script cannot write its `attr`.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Players.Playe.documentation:
PlayerAdded fires with each player that joins. On the server, every `PlayerAdded` handler runs before `CharacterAdded` fires for that player. On a client, it fires only for players who join after the client scripts start.

Read only at runtime.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Players.Playe.code_sample:
-- Server script: show Points on the player list.
game.Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
    local stats = Instance.new("leaderstats")
    stats.attr.Points = 0
    stats.Parent = player
end)

@luduvo/server/global/game.Players.Playe.documentation:
PlayerChatted fires with the speaker and the text of each chat message.

Read only at runtime.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Players.Playe.code_sample:
-- Server script.
game.Players.PlayerChatted:Connect(function(player, message)
    if message == "!ready" then
        player.attr.Ready = true
    end
end)

@luduvo/server/global/game.Players.Playe.documentation:
PlayerRemoving fires with each player that leaves, and for every player when the server shuts down. On shutdown, the world waits up to 30 seconds for `CloudStore` requests started before the handler yields, so a handler can save player data.

Read only at runtime.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Players.Playe.code_sample:
-- Server script.
game.Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
    print(player.Name .. " left with " .. (player.attr.Points or 0) .. " points")
end)

@luduvo/server/global/game.Prefabs.documentation:
Prefabs spawns copies of prefabs and resets edited copies to their prefab's values. A prefab is a saved tree of instances that Studio exports with File > Export Selection... to an `.ldv` file named after the prefab.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Prefabs.Exist.documentation: Exists returns whether the place or the platform has a prefab named `name`.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Prefabs.Exist.code_sample:
-- Server script.
if game.Prefabs.Exists("TreasureChest") then
    local chest = game.Prefabs.Spawn("TreasureChest")
    if chest then
        chest.Position = Vector3.new(0, 2, 10)
    end
end

@luduvo/server/global/game.Prefabs.Id.documentation: Id returns the numeric id of the prefab `name`, or 0 when there is none. The root of a spawned copy has this id in its `PrefabId` property.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Prefabs.Id.code_sample:
-- Server script.
local bulletId = game.Prefabs.Id("Bullet")
local bullet = game.Prefabs.Spawn("Bullet")
-- compare numbers instead of names
if bullet and bullet.PrefabId == bulletId then
    bullet.Position = Vector3.new(0, 5, 0)
end

@luduvo/server/global/game.Prefabs.Name.documentation: Name returns the name of the prefab with numeric id `id`, or `nil` when there is none.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Prefabs.Name.code_sample:
-- Server script.
local crate = game.Prefabs.Spawn("Crate")
if crate then
    -- look up the prefab name from the copy
    local prefabName = game.Prefabs.Name(crate.PrefabId)
    if prefabName then
        crate.Name = prefabName .. "Copy"
    end
end

@luduvo/server/global/game.Prefabs.Rever.documentation: RevertAddedComponent removes a component that a script or Studio added to an instance of a prefab copy. To reset a component that the prefab has, use RevertObjectOverride.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Prefabs.Rever.code_sample:
-- Server script.
local gate = game.Prefabs.Spawn("Gate")
if gate then
    gate:AddComponent("Anchored")
    -- remove the added component
    game.Prefabs.RevertAddedComponent(gate, "Anchored")
end

@luduvo/server/global/game.Prefabs.Rever.documentation: RevertObjectOverride resets every component shared by `entity` and the prefab to the prefab's values. It leaves children, added or removed components, and tags unchanged.
notes: On the root of the copy, `Name`, `Position`, rotation, `LocalTransform`, and `Pivot` keep their values.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Prefabs.Rever.code_sample:
-- Server script.
local door = game.Prefabs.Spawn("Door")
if door then
    door.Size = Vector3.new(10, 10, 10)
    -- restore the prefab's size
    game.Prefabs.RevertObjectOverride(door)
end

@luduvo/server/global/game.Prefabs.Spawn.documentation: Spawn creates a copy of the prefab `name` and returns its root, or `nil` when no prefab has that name. It places the root at the top of the place, at the position saved in the prefab.
notes: On a client, `Spawn` spawns only platform prefabs and returns `nil` for place prefabs, though `Exists` and `Id` also find place prefabs there.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Prefabs.Spawn.code_sample:
-- Server script.
local enemy = game.Prefabs.Spawn("Goblin")
if enemy then
    -- move the copy to its spawn point
    enemy.Position = Vector3.new(24, 0, -50)
end

@luduvo/server/global/game.Profiler.documentation:
Profiler reads frame times and per-script times on the machine that runs the script. To time one block of code, use `tick`.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Profiler.Drop.documentation: Dropped returns how many script runs went unrecorded because Scripts already had 64 entries.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Profiler.Drop.code_sample:
-- Server script.
task.wait(10)
if game.Profiler.Dropped() > 0 then
    warn("more scripts run than the profiler tracks")
end

@luduvo/server/global/game.Profiler.Fram.documentation: Frame returns a `FrameStats` table for the last finished frame, or `nil` before the first frame ends.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Profiler.Fram.code_sample:
-- Server script.
function Update(dt)
    local stats = game.Profiler.Frame()
    if stats and stats.interval > 50 then
        warn(string.format("slow frame: %d ms", math.round(stats.interval)))
    end
end

@luduvo/server/global/game.Profiler.Scri.documentation: Scripts returns a `ScriptCost` table for each of up to 64 scripts that ran recently, in no fixed order.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Profiler.Scri.code_sample:
-- Server script: print the slowest script every 5 seconds.
while true do
    task.wait(5)
    local slowest = nil
    for _, cost in game.Profiler.Scripts() do
        if not slowest or cost.avg > slowest.avg then
            slowest = cost
        end
    end
    if slowest then
        print(slowest.path, slowest.avg)
    end
end

@luduvo/server/global/game.Session.documentation:
Session reports the place, the server clock, and the connection of this client. All of its functions and signals are deprecated; use Players instead.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Session.BindC.documentation:
BindCharacter makes `character` the character of the player `userId`.

Server only.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Session.Chara.documentation:
CharacterDied fires with the dead character, its owner's user id, and the attacker; each may be `nil`.

Read only at runtime.
CharacterOf returns the character of the player `userId`, or `nil`.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Session.Kick.documentation:
Kick disconnects the player `userId` at the end of the current server step.

Server only.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Session.Playe.documentation:
PlayerJoined fires with the user id of each player who joins.

Read only at runtime.

PlayerLeft fires with the character, or `nil`, and the user id of each player who leaves.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Session.Serve.documentation:
ServerTick is the network tick of the server. On a client it estimates the current server tick, with a fractional part, and reads `0` until its first clock sample, a few frames after joining.

Read only at runtime.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Session.Serve.code_sample:
-- Server script.
-- count the network ticks of a one-second wait
local start = game.Session.ServerTick
task.wait(1)
print(game.Session.ServerTick - start)

@luduvo/server/global/game.Session.Serve.documentation:
ServerTime is ServerTick divided by TickRate, the server clock in seconds.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Session.TickR.documentation:
TickRate is the number of network ticks the server runs per second.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Sound.documentation:
Sound plays one-shot sounds at world positions and sets how loud touching parts sound. For a sound that loops or needs Play and Stop, use a `Sound` instance or a `Sound` component on a part instead.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Sound.GetBusV.documentation: GetBusVolumeDb returns the volume of a mixer bus in decibels.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Sound.PlayAt.documentation: PlayAt plays a one-shot sound at a world position, with a volume from 0 to 1. Pass the asset id as a string: a number cannot represent every digit of a 64-bit id. It plays at full volume within 10 units and fades to 1/20 at 200 units. The server does not send it to players whose character is farther than 200 units away.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Sound.PlayAt.code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: play a chime at the part every 2 seconds.
local CHIME = "144115188075855954" -- an audio asset id
while true do
    game.Sound.PlayAt(CHIME, self.Position, 0.8)
    task.wait(2)
end

@luduvo/server/global/game.Sound.SetBusV.documentation: SetBusVolumeDb sets the volume of a mixer bus in decibels.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Sound.SetBusV.deprecation: Write the `MasterVolume`, `MusicVolume`, `SFXVolume`, and `UIVolume` fields of the `SoundConfig` singleton through World.Query.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Sound.Surface.documentation: SurfaceSoundsVolume is the volume of the impact and sliding sounds of touching parts, from 0 (silent) to 1.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Store.documentation:
Store saves tables by key to disk on the server machine, so they survive a server restart. Use `game.CloudStore` when players need their data across servers.

Server only.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Store.open.documentation:
open opens or creates the store `name` and returns its `Store` handle. Opening the same name again returns the same store.

Server only.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Store.open.code_sample:
-- Server script: count how many times this server has started.
local stats = game.Store.open("server_stats")
local data = stats:get(1) or { starts = 0 }
data.starts += 1
stats:put(1, data)
print("starts: " .. data.starts) -- prints "starts: 1" the first time

@luduvo/server/global/game.String.documentation:
String is the field type of a string of at most 64 bytes with no zero byte.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Tags.documentation:
Tags signals when instances gain or lose a tag. A tag is a name with no fields, added with `instance:AddComponent(game.World.Pair("Tag", name))` and found with World.Each or World.Query and the same pair. Tags replicate to clients and save with the place.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Tags.Add.documentation: Add adds a tag to an instance.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Tags.Find.documentation: Find returns every instance that has a tag.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Tags.Find.deprecation: Use World.Each or World.Query with `game.World.Pair("Tag", tag)`.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Tags.Get.documentation: Get returns the tag names on an instance.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Tags.GetInsta.documentation: GetInstanceAddedSignal returns a signal that fires with each instance that gains the tag, including tagged instances that spawn or replicate.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Tags.GetInsta.code_sample:
-- Server script: print each part that becomes an enemy.
game.Tags.GetInstanceAddedSignal("Enemy"):Connect(function(enemy: Instance)
    print(enemy.Name .. " is an enemy")
end)

local goblin = Instance.new("Part")
goblin.Name = "Goblin"
goblin:AddComponent(game.World.Pair("Tag", "Enemy")) -- prints "Goblin is an enemy"

@luduvo/server/global/game.Tags.GetInsta.documentation: GetInstanceRemovedSignal returns a signal that fires with each instance that loses the tag or is destroyed while it has the tag.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Tags.GetInsta.code_sample:
-- Server script: keep a set of live enemies.
local enemies: { [Instance]: boolean } = {}

game.Tags.GetInstanceAddedSignal("Enemy"):Connect(function(enemy: Instance)
    enemies[enemy] = true
end)
game.Tags.GetInstanceRemovedSignal("Enemy"):Connect(function(enemy: Instance)
    enemies[enemy] = nil -- a destroyed instance still works as a key
    print("enemy gone")
end)

local goblin = Instance.new("Part")
goblin:AddComponent(game.World.Pair("Tag", "Enemy"))
task.wait(1)
goblin:Destroy() -- prints "enemy gone"

@luduvo/server/global/game.Tags.Has.documentation: Has returns whether an instance has a tag.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Tags.Remove.documentation: Remove removes a tag from an instance.

@luduvo/server/global/game.ToClients.documentation:
ToClients is the direction of a table whose events go from the server to clients. Server scripts fire them with `FireAllClients` or `FireClient`.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.ToServer.documentation:
ToServer is the direction of a table whose events go from clients to the server. Client scripts fire them with `FireServer`, and the server gets each event with the player who sent it. The server drops the whole packet and disconnects the player if a packet has malformed data, a non-finite number or a boolean byte above 1.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Tween.documentation:
Tween animates a property from its current value to a target value over time.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Tween.TweenPr.documentation: TweenProperty animates a property of an instance to `final` over `duration` seconds and returns a `Tween` handle.
notes: Writes the property after `Update` callbacks run, so it overrides a script that writes the same property in that frame.
When the tween starts, it ends any older tween on the same property.
@luduvo/server/global/game.Tween.TweenPr.code_sample:
-- Server script.
local platform = Instance.new("Part")
platform.Anchored = true
platform.Position = Vector3.new(0, 10, 0)

-- slide 20 units along x in 3 seconds
local tween = game.Tween.TweenProperty(platform, "Position", Vector3.new(20, 10, 0), 3)
tween:SetTrans("Sine")
tween.Finished:Connect(function()
    platform.Transparency = 0.5
end)

@luduvo/server/global/game.U8.documentation:
U8 is the field type of a whole number from 0 to 255. A sent number clamps to that range and loses its fraction.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.Vec3.documentation:
Vec3 is the field type of a vector of three 32-bit floats. In a `ToServer` event, the server drops the packet on NaN or infinity.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/game.World.documentation:
World is the top of the place's tree of parts and entities. It also runs queries over scene entities and schedules per-frame systems. The server and each client have their own world, and a call acts on the world of the side that makes it.

Read only at runtime.

@luduvo/server/global/geometry.documentation: geometry splits flat 2D outlines into triangles, for meshes a script builds.

@luduvo/server/global/geometry.triangula.documentation: `geometry.triangulate_polygon` splits a polygon of `count` points into triangles. `points` has two 32-bit floats (x, y) per point, and `indices` receives three 32-bit indices per triangle, counterclockwise. It returns the number of indices written, or 0 when it cannot split the outline.
@luduvo/server/global/geometry.triangula.code_sample:
-- Server script: split a square outline into two triangles.
local corners = { 0, 0, 10, 0, 10, 10, 0, 10 }
local points = buffer.create(#corners * 4)
for i, value in corners do
    buffer.writef32(points, (i - 1) * 4, value)
end

local indices = buffer.create(6 * 4)
print(geometry.triangulate_polygon(points, 4, indices)) -- prints 6

@luduvo/server/global/handles.documentation: `handles` is a table of the instances picked for the script's instance in Studio, keyed by slot name. The engine fills it once, when the script starts: a slot with no target or an already-destroyed target is `nil`, while a target destroyed later stays in the table as a destroyed instance.
@luduvo/server/global/handles.code_sample:
-- Server script in a part with handle slots Door and Switch.
local door = handles.Door
local switch = handles.Switch
if not door or not switch then
    return
end

switch.Touched:Connect(function()
    door.Transparency = 0.5
    door.Position = door.Position + Vector3.new(0, 4, 0)
end)

@luduvo/server/global/plugin.documentation: `plugin` is the Studio plugin whose `init.lua` is running, and `nil` in every other script. Studio runs `init.lua` on its own server with the server script API. Call `Operator`, `Tool` and `Ribbon` while `init.lua` runs; if it raises an error or waits, Studio disables the plugin. Plugin code changes the place only through `ctx.Edit` in an operator's `Execute`, so Undo takes back each run as one step.
@luduvo/server/global/plugin.code_sample:
-- init.lua of a Studio plugin.
plugin:Operator({
    Id = "build.raise",
    Label = "Raise",
    Tooltip = "Lift the selected parts by the move increment",
    Params = {
        { Name = "Parts", Type = "instances", Hidden = true, From = "Selection" },
        { Name = "Height", Type = "number", Default = "MoveIncrement" },
    },
    Poll = function(ctx: PluginContext)
        if #ctx.Selection == 0 then
            return false, "Select the parts to raise"
        end
        return true
    end,
    Execute = function(ctx: PluginContext, params)
        local edit = ctx.Edit :: PluginEdit
        for _, part: Instance in params.Parts do
            edit:Set(part, "Position", part.Position + Vector3.new(0, params.Height, 0))
        end
        return true
    end,
})

plugin:Ribbon({ Group = "Build", Items = { "build.raise" } })

@luduvo/server/global/print.documentation: print writes its arguments, separated by tabs, to Output and the in-game console (F9). A game server sends players' consoles at most 256 lines or 32768 bytes a second from server scripts and drops the rest.
@luduvo/server/global/print.code_sample:
-- Server script.
print("score", 10, true) -- prints score    10  true

@luduvo/server/global/rotation.documentation: rotation builds, combines and converts rotation vectors. Each vector points along the axis of the turn, and its length is the angle in radians. A positive angle turns counterclockwise as seen from the tip of the axis. An unrotated instance faces -Z, with +Y up. `Orientation` is in degrees, so convert with to_euler and from_euler, or use RotationVector and PivotTo, which take rotation vectors.

@luduvo/server/global/rotation.apply.documentation: `rotation.apply` turns the vector `v` by the rotation `r`.
@luduvo/server/global/rotation.apply.code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: launch it forward the way it faces.
self.Anchored = false
local facing = rotation.from_euler(self.Orientation)
self.Velocity = rotation.apply(facing, Vector3.new(0, 0, -30))

@luduvo/server/global/rotation.axis.documentation: `rotation.axis` returns the rotation by `angle` radians about `axis`.
@luduvo/server/global/rotation.axis.code_sample:
-- Server script in a propeller part: spin about Z twice a second.
local angle = 0

function Update(dt: number)
    angle += 4 * math.pi * dt
    self.Orientation = rotation.to_euler(rotation.axis(Vector3.zAxis, angle))
end

@luduvo/server/global/rotation.compose.documentation: `rotation.compose` returns the rotation that turns by `b` first, then by `a`.
@luduvo/server/global/rotation.compose.code_sample:
-- Server script in a turret part: tilt 10 degrees up, then turn 45 degrees left.
local yaw = rotation.axis(Vector3.yAxis, math.rad(45))
local pitch = rotation.axis(Vector3.xAxis, math.rad(10))
self.Orientation = rotation.to_euler(rotation.compose(yaw, pitch))

@luduvo/server/global/rotation.from_eule.documentation: `rotation.from_euler` converts an `Orientation` in degrees into a rotation vector.
@luduvo/server/global/rotation.from_eule.code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
self.Orientation = Vector3.new(0, 90, 0)
local facing = rotation.apply(rotation.from_euler(self.Orientation), Vector3.new(0, 0, -1))
print(math.round(facing.X)) -- prints -1

@luduvo/server/global/rotation.look.documentation: `rotation.look` returns the rotation that points -Z along `forward` with +Y as close to `up` (`Vector3.yAxis` by default) as it can.
@luduvo/server/global/rotation.look.code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: face the world origin.
local direction = Vector3.zero - self.Position
if direction.Magnitude > 0 then
    self.Orientation = rotation.to_euler(rotation.look(direction))
end

@luduvo/server/global/rotation.slerp.documentation: `rotation.slerp` blends from rotation `a` at `t` 0 to rotation `b` at `t` 1 along the shortest turn.
@luduvo/server/global/rotation.slerp.code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: swing a quarter turn over 2 seconds.
local from = rotation.from_euler(self.Orientation)
local to = rotation.compose(rotation.axis(Vector3.yAxis, math.pi / 2), from)
local elapsed = 0

function Update(dt: number)
    elapsed = math.min(elapsed + dt, 2)
    self.Orientation = rotation.to_euler(rotation.slerp(from, to, elapsed / 2))
end

@luduvo/server/global/rotation.to_euler.documentation: `rotation.to_euler` converts a rotation vector into an `Orientation` in degrees.
@luduvo/server/global/rotation.to_euler.code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: face 30 degrees to the left.
self.Orientation = rotation.to_euler(rotation.axis(Vector3.yAxis, math.rad(30)))
print(math.round(self.Orientation.Y)) -- prints 30

@luduvo/server/global/self.documentation: `self` is the instance that runs the script, usually the part the script is attached to. Every script on that instance gets the same `self`. In a script under `scripts/autorun/`, `self` is `nil`; see scripts that run for the whole place.
@luduvo/server/global/self.code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: the part disappears when something touches it.
self.Touched:Connect(function()
    self:Destroy()
end)

@luduvo/server/global/shared.documentation: `shared` is a table that all server scripts, or all client scripts of one player, read and write. It works like `_G`, except that reading an unset name gives `nil` instead of a built-in global.
@luduvo/server/global/shared.code_sample:
-- Server script.
shared.SpawnInterval = shared.SpawnInterval or 2
print(shared.print) -- prints nil

@luduvo/server/global/task.documentation: task runs functions later or in their own threads, and pauses the running thread. Scheduled threads belong to the calling script: the engine drops them if the script reloads or its instance is destroyed. Waits and delays count update ticks, so they end on the first tick at or after the time.

@luduvo/server/global/task.cancel.documentation: `task.cancel` stops a thread from `task.delay`, `task.defer` or `task.spawn` so it never resumes.
@luduvo/server/global/task.cancel.code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: despawn in 30 seconds unless something touches it.
local despawn = task.delay(30, function()
    self:Destroy()
end)

self.Touched:Connect(function()
    task.cancel(despawn)
end)

@luduvo/server/global/task.defer.documentation: `task.defer` runs a function at the end of this tick, after every `Update`, and returns its thread.

@luduvo/server/global/task.delay.documentation: `task.delay` runs a function after `seconds`, and returns its thread.
@luduvo/server/global/task.delay.code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: the part disappears after 2 seconds.
task.delay(2, function()
    self:Destroy()
end)

@luduvo/server/global/task.spawn.documentation: `task.spawn` runs a function at once, until it waits or ends, and returns its thread. An error in the function logs a `Task error` warning and does not stop the caller.
@luduvo/server/global/task.spawn.code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: blink while the rest of the script goes on.
task.spawn(function()
    while true do
        self.Transparency = 1
        task.wait(0.5)
        self.Transparency = 0
        task.wait(0.5)
    end
end)
print("blinking")

@luduvo/server/global/task.wait.documentation: `task.wait` pauses the running thread for at least `seconds`, or one tick when `seconds` is left out, and returns the seconds that passed.
notes: `Update`, `PhysicsUpdate` and `World.System` callbacks cannot wait; start the waiting code with `task.spawn` instead.
A script finishes loading at its first top-level wait, so declare `Update`, `PhysicsUpdate` and `Migrate` before it; see `Update`.
@luduvo/server/global/task.wait.code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: a platform that moves up and down every 3 seconds.
local low = self.Position
local high = low + Vector3.new(0, 6, 0)

while true do
    task.wait(3)
    self.Position = high
    task.wait(3)
    self.Position = low
end

@luduvo/server/global/tick.documentation: tick returns the time in seconds from a clock that only moves forward. Subtract two readings to measure how long something took.
@luduvo/server/global/tick.code_sample:
-- Server script: time a loop.
local start = tick()
local sum = 0
for i = 1, 100000 do
    sum += i
end
print("took", tick() - start, "seconds")

@luduvo/server/global/warn.documentation: warn writes its arguments to the output as a warning, like `print`. The script keeps running.
@luduvo/server/global/warn.code_sample:
-- Server script.
local config: { [string]: number } = { MaxPlayers = 8 }
if config.SpawnInterval == nil then
    warn("SpawnInterval is missing; using 2 seconds")
end

@luduvo/server/globaltype/AnimPreviewInf.documentation: AnimPreviewInfo is the state of a character's animation preview, returned by Instance:AnimationPreview.
clip is the name of the previewed clip, or nil if the clip has no name.
playing is true while the preview plays and false while it is paused.
shared is true if something else changed the character's pose after the preview set it.
speed is the playback multiplier from 0 to 10; 1 is normal speed.
time is the preview's position in the clip, in seconds.

@luduvo/server/globaltype/CloudStore.documentation: CloudStore is a collection of records shared by every server of the game, opened with `CloudStore.open`. See CloudStore for the request budget and size limits.

@luduvo/server/globaltype/CloudStore.fet.documentation: fetch loads the table saved under a key. The callback gets the table, its version and nil; `(nil, 0, nil)` if the key has no record; or an error string as the third value if the request failed.
@luduvo/server/globaltype/CloudStore.fet.code_sample:
-- Server script.
local profiles = game.CloudStore.open("profiles")

game.Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player: Instance)
    profiles:fetch(player.UserId, function(data, version, err)
        if err then
            warn("could not load profile: " .. err)
            return
        end
        player.attr.Gold = if data then data.gold else 0
    end)
end)

@luduvo/server/globaltype/CloudStore.key.documentation: keys lists the keys of the store in key order, at most `limit` (up to 100) per call. Pass the last key of one page as `after` to get the next page.
@luduvo/server/globaltype/CloudStore.key.code_sample:
-- Server script.
local profiles = game.CloudStore.open("profiles")

local function listFrom(after: string?)
    profiles:keys(after, 100, function(keys, err)
        for _, key in keys do
            print(key)
        end
        if not err and #keys == 100 then
            listFrom(keys[#keys])
        end
    end)
end

listFrom(nil)

@luduvo/server/globaltype/CloudStore.put.documentation: put saves a table under a key, replacing the record there. Pass a version from `fetch` as `expect_version` to fail with `"conflict"` if another server wrote first, or nil to write regardless. The callback gets the new version, or nil and an error string.

@luduvo/server/globaltype/CloudStore.rem.documentation: remove deletes the record saved under a key. The callback gets true if a record was deleted.
@luduvo/server/globaltype/CloudStore.rem.code_sample:
-- Server script: delete the profile of user 42.
local profiles = game.CloudStore.open("profiles")

profiles:remove(42)

@luduvo/server/globaltype/CloudStore.upd.documentation: update loads a record, passes it to `transform`, and saves the table `transform` returns, or nothing if it returns nil. If another server saved the key in between, `transform` runs again on the newer record, up to 3 more times, so keep it free of other effects.

@luduvo/server/globaltype/ColorSequence.documentation: ColorSequence is an immutable curve of colors over time from 0 to 1, read from a component field of type `ColorSequence`. To change a field, assign a new sequence from `ColorSequence.new`. A field that was never assigned reads as constant white.
@luduvo/server/globaltype/ColorSequence.code_sample:
-- Server script.
local fade = ColorSequence.new(Color3.new(1, 1, 1), Color3.new(0, 0, 0))

print(#fade.Keypoints) -- prints 2
print(fade) -- prints ColorSequence(0 1 1 1, 1 0 0 0)

@luduvo/server/globaltype/ColorSequence..documentation: Keypoints is a new array of the sequence's 2 to 8 keypoints in time order.
__eq returns true if both sequences have the same keypoints.
__tostring returns the time, red, green and blue of each keypoint.

@luduvo/server/globaltype/ColorSequenceK.documentation: ColorSequenceKeypoint is one immutable point of a `ColorSequence`: a color at a time.
@luduvo/server/globaltype/ColorSequenceK.code_sample:
-- Server script.
local fade = ColorSequence.new(Color3.new(1, 0.5, 0), Color3.new(0, 0, 0))
local first = fade.Keypoints[1]

print(first.Time) -- prints 0
